title: Introduction to Algebra
ebookHtml:
1. Core Algebra Foundations

Algebra uses symbols (like x, y, and z) to represent numbers and express general mathematical relationships. In this introductory lesson, we will cover the basics of variables, terms, coefficients, and operations.

Why Study Algebra?

Algebra is the language of science, physics, and computer modeling. By substituting numbers with variables, we can formulate general rules to solve problems.

title: Linear Equations & Graphing
description: Solving single variable equations and plotting slopes
ebookHtml:
2. Graphing Straight Lines

A linear function plots a straight line on a graph. The standard slope-intercept form is represented as:

y = mx + c

Where m represents the steepness (slope) of the line, and c is the y-intercept where the line intersects the vertical y-axis.

title: Quadratic Equations
description: Learning the quadratic formula and factoring
ebookHtml:
3. The Quadratic Formula

For any second-degree polynomial equation of the form:

ax² + bx + c = 0

The roots (solutions) can be determined using the quadratic formula:

x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a
